currentContext.business: The Company owns, develops and asset-manages hotels, resorts and serviced residences that are operated under third-party global hotel flags, and separately owns and leases office and retail space that sits alongside those hotels in mixed-use destinations. The AR states it 'participates across the full asset lifecycle, from development and strategic positioning to operations and long-term performance management' and that its 'integrated approach allows us to create dynamic mixed-use destinations where hospitality, commercial, and retail spaces strengthen one another, driving embedded demand and enhancing asset value'. Customers span B2B (hotel brand partners under whose flags it operates, corporates contracting bulk crew accommodation, corporate tenants of leased commercial space) and B2C (in-house guests at hotels and serviced apartments, F&B patrons, retail tenants and walk-in customers at mixed-use developments). BRSR Section A names two activities accounting for 90% of turnover: 'Accommodation and Food Services' (NIC 551) at 79% of turnover and 'Real Estate — real estate activities with own or leased property' (NIC 701) at 19.04%.

currentContext.expansion: Ventive's expansion is asset acquisition and key addition, not plant capex. WITHIN FY 2025-26 the Board's Report records two completed acquisitions: (i) a 76% stake in Soham Leisure Ventures Private Limited, 'the owning entity of Hilton Goa Resort', on 15th October 2025, making it a subsidiary; and (ii) through material step-down subsidiary Panchshil Corporate Park Private Limited, a 100% stake in Finest-VN Business Park Private Limited on 17 February 2026 - Finest-VN 'through its subsidiaries, holds the exclusive rights for the expansion of Soho House in India and operates Soho House Mumbai (Juhu)'. AFTER the financial year, two further acquisitions closed: Soham acquired 100% of Sun Leisure India Private Limited, owner of the hotel Sol de Goa, and Panchshil Corporate Park acquired 50.02% of Narmada Estates Private Limited. The consolidated accounts add the mechanics of both (back-filled with provenance from the governance_entities sibling bundle, Note 51): the Narmada SPA is dated 15th April 2026 for a 50.02% equity stake 'for a total consideration of J 886.80 million', and 'Narmada owns a land parcel in the vicinity of the existing hotel of PCPPL, "The Ritz-Carlton, Pune'; the Sun Leisure SPA is dated 7th April 2026 for 100% 'for a total consideration of J 5.00 million'. The milestone spread frames the trajectory: '~2x Growth in keys - From 1,164 keys in 2021 to 2,199 keys in 2026 ... with a clear roadmap to achieve ~4,000 keys by 2031', with 2025 marked by the 'Signing of new hotels comprising 1,382 keys with Marriott International in India and Sri Lanka'. THE DECLARED PIPELINE (from the Geographical Presence spread, back-filled with provenance from the profile sibling bundle) is: Moxy Pune Wakad 264 keys; Moxy Pune Kharadi 200 keys; AC by Marriott, Bengaluru - 166 keys rebranding of the existing Aloft Bengaluru Whitefield plus 33 additional keys; JW Marriott Navi Mumbai 450 keys; Moxy Navi Mumbai 200 keys; Soho House New Delhi (Mehrauli) 24 keys; Varanasi Marriott Hotel 161 keys; the commercial annuity asset Narmada Estates, Pune 0.63 msf; and in Sri Lanka, Pottuvil, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, with 73 villas plus 80 branded residences. Within the existing portfolio, Hilton Goa Resort (104 keys) is printed as 'expanding key count by ~50+ keys and branded luxury villas'. The AR disclaims that 'the proposed key counts are indicative in nature and are subject to change as the projects advance' and that the brand names 'represent hotel brands expected to be added to the Company's portfolio and are for indicative purposes only' - no commissioning or completion date is attached to ANY of these projects anywhere in the routed text. Two owned entities are still pre-operational: 'NAGENAHIRA RESORTS (PVT) LTD and KBJ HOTEL & RESTAURANTS PRIVATE LIMITED is yet to commence operations'. Structural expansion is also being pursued through corporate action: a scheme of amalgamation of EON-Hinjewadi Infrastructure, Restocraft Hospitality and Wellcraft Infraprojects into Ventive Hospitality Limited was filed with the NCLT on 12th September 2025. On the geography of future build-out, the 'Building Pune's Hospitality Future' chapter states that 'our future hospitality pipeline in the city is positioned to support the next phase of this expansion' by 'adding capacity, strengthening our presence across high-potential locations, and deepening the city's premium hospitality infrastructure', citing Pune's 500+ GCCs expected to grow to 660-680 by 2030 and office space rising from 100 million sq. ft. to 145 million sq. ft. by 2030 (KPMG). The only capex-composition figure disclosed in narrative form is from BRSR Principle 2: '9.71% of the Company's total capital expenditure for FY 2025-26 was directed towards technologies that improve environmental and social impacts, principally renewable energy (rooftop solar PV), energy-efficient HVAC and heat-pump systems, low-GWP refrigeration, smart building controls and metering, wastewater treatment and water-recycling infrastructure, and fire and life-safety systems' (prior year: 0). R&D capex is a stated nil - 'The Company hasn't carried a formal research and development function or associated expenditure.' The rupee capex quantum arrived only as NAMED DISCLOSURE blocks that are defective and therefore NOT carried into capex_disclosed - see notes.
currentContext.mdna: India macro: GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2026 against 7.1% in FY 2025 (MoSPI new series, base 2022-23), supported by strong domestic demand, policy reforms and recovering private and public investment; 'sectors such as trade, hotels, transport, and communication witnessed a strong recovery'. The RBI cut the repo rate in phases as inflation eased.|Rising per-capita income is cited as a demand driver - 'per capita income has been rising and is expected to increase from $ 2,675 in 2025 to $ 3,075 in 2027' - alongside urbanisation, a young workforce and an expanding middle class.|Global tourism outlook for 2026 remains positive with tourism 'expected to grow by 3-4% year-over-year', helped by the FIFA World Cup 2026 and the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics; offsetting factors named are geopolitical tensions, high travel costs, economic uncertainty and a traveller shift toward value for money. International tourist arrivals reached ~1.52 Bn in 2025, +4% over 2024 and above pre-pandemic levels; Asia-Pacific ITAs ~331 Mn, +6%.|Indian hospitality is structurally undersupplied - 'an undersupplied market in which demand outpaced available room inventory' - with 2025 occupancy 64% (+1.1 pts), ADR H 8,624 (+8.6%) and RevPAR H 5,522 (+10.8%). Branded inventory ~133,000 rooms; total inventory ~216,000 rooms (+7.7% YoY); pipeline expanded by 39,000 rooms to 144,000, implying ~360,000 rooms by 2030 if all planned projects complete.|GCC-led corporate demand is the named new demand pool: GCCs 'attract large volumes of business travel, long-stay corporate guests, training visits, client meetings, and relocation-related stays' in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Delhi-NCR, lifting weekday occupancy and stabilising year-round demand across mid-scale to luxury.|Pune - the Company's flagship market - is described as supply-constrained at the top end: room supply grew only 757 rooms since 2019 against 654 rooms of demand growth, Lux-Upper Upscale ADR crossed H 10,000 in 2025, city-wide occupancy reached 70.5% (strongest among India's non-metro business markets), and 'the forward supply pipeline contains no new luxury hotels and only modest Upper Upscale rooms'. Pune city 2025 metrics: ~70.5% occupancy, ADR ~H 7,000, RevPAR ~H 5,000. Future connectivity from the Navi Mumbai International Airport and better road infrastructure is expected to help.|Maldives market sizing: valued at ~$2.87 Bn in 2025, projected $3.13 Bn in 2026 and $4.78 Bn by 2031 at 8.87% CAGR (Mordor Intelligence). Luxury held the largest share at 51.24% in 2025 and is expected to grow at 11.37% CAGR to 2031; independent hotels held 57.87% share while chain hotels are expected to grow at 9.29% CAGR. Supportive: Velana International Airport upgrades, new direct long-haul routes, government incentives and faster approvals. Structural negatives named: high import dependency and climate vulnerability.|Demand-mix drivers named for India: business travel, MICE, weddings, hybrid travel and workcations lengthening average stays and improving asset utilisation, and premiumisation from rising disposable incomes and preference for premium experiences, luxury stays and wellness tourism.|Segment-mix backdrop: Luxury and Upper Upscale account for more than 20% of room inventory in most markets (lower in Mumbai), with Goa ~45% and Jaipur ~55%.|Forward supply concentration to watch, 2026-2030: Bengaluru is expected to lead with ~11,400 new rooms and Delhi NCR ~9,300 - both markets where the Company has existing or upcoming assets.|India international tourist arrivals moderated - 20.09 Mn in 2025 (provisional) versus 20.57 Mn in 2024, a 2.4% decline from a high base - a stated negative within an otherwise positive demand narrative.|Company-level positioning statement in the Board's Report: 'With a diversified portfolio across India and the Maldives and exposure to both high-growth domestic demand and premium international leisure destinations, Ventive Hospitality is well-positioned to benefit from sustained industry tailwinds and the continued shift towards luxury, experience-led travel.'|Management's own framing of the international backdrop: 'global travel demand witnessed periods of uncertainty during the year, influenced by evolving geopolitical developments, including tensions in parts of the Middle East. However, demand across our international portfolio remained resilient' - with 'supply-side constraints in premium segments' expected to support long-term value creation. [profile sibling bundle - Management Message.]|Hospitality has no order book; the analogue disclosed is the development pipeline. Upcoming projects printed in the 'Geographical Presence' spread: Moxy Pune Wakad (264 keys), Moxy Pune Kharadi (200 keys), AC by Marriott Bengaluru (166 keys rebranding + 33 additional keys), JW Marriott Navi Mumbai (450 keys), Moxy Navi Mumbai (200 keys), Soho House New Delhi, Mehrauli (24 keys), Varanasi Marriott Hotel (161 keys), the commercial annuity asset Narmada Estates, Pune (0.63 msf), and Pottuvil, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Sri Lanka (73 villas + 80 branded residences). The AR disclaims that 'the proposed key counts are indicative in nature and are subject to change as the projects advance' and that the brand names 'represent hotel brands expected to be added ... and are for indicative purposes only'. [Back-filled with provenance from the profile sibling bundle.]|Signed pipeline with a named counterparty: 'Signing of new hotels comprising 1,382 keys with Marriott International in India and Sri Lanka' (2025 milestone). [Back-filled with provenance from the capex_expansion sibling bundle - milestones spread.]|Stated roadmap: '~2x Growth in keys - From 1,164 keys in 2021 to 2,199 keys in 2026 ... with a clear roadmap to achieve ~4,000 keys by 2031.' [capex_expansion sibling bundle.]|Two owned entities are pre-operational and therefore represent committed but unearning capacity: 'NAGENAHIRA RESORTS (PVT) LTD and KBJ HOTEL & RESTAURANTS PRIVATE LIMITED is yet to commence operations'. [profile/registry sibling bundles - BRSR Section A.]

risks.risk: Physical climate risk to coastal and island assets
risks.note: Flagged by the Company as a RISK with negative financial implications: 'Our high-value assets in coastal and island settings - Goa and the Maldives - face cyclones, storm surge and long-term sea-level rise, while our inland properties in Pune contend with urban flooding. A single severe event can damage property, disrupt operations, inflate insurance premiums and keep guests away in peak season.' Mitigation stated as climate-resilient specifications in new construction and major refurbishments, insurance updated against climate-adjusted loss models, climate-risk assumptions embedded in capital-expenditure decisions and physical-risk findings fed into the Board-level Risk Management framework. Structural because 515 of 2,199 keys are Maldivian island resorts and the newest India growth vector is coastal Goa.

risks.risk: Water availability, tariffs and discharge compliance
risks.note: Flagged as a RISK with negative implications: the Company operates 'from the water-stressed basins of Pune to island resorts in the Maldives that rely on energy-intensive desalination', and 'shrinking freshwater availability, rising municipal tariffs and tightening discharge norms make water both a material cost and a question of operational continuity'. Explicitly: 'any lapse against discharge norms would expose us to penalties.' Mitigation includes sewage treatment plants at all operational properties by FY 2026-27, reuse for landscaping/cooling/flushing, rainwater harvesting, greywater recycling and brine management at SWRO-equipped island resorts.

Energy is stated to be 'among our largest operating costs' - hotels, offices and retail draw power continuously for HVAC, kitchens, laundry, lighting and shared areas - and 'a significant share still flows from the grid, leaving us exposed to tariff volatility and weighing materially on our Scope 2 footprint'. Framed by the Company as an opportunity, but the exposure to tariff volatility is a structural cost risk for an owner of energy-intensive luxury assets.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety, with incomplete certification coverage
risks.note: Flagged as a RISK with negative implications: hotels carry 'a wide range of hazards - across kitchens, chemical handling, fire systems, electrical installations, pools and high-footfall public spaces - and a safety failure carries human, regulatory and reputational consequences'. Critically, the Company concedes that although it operates under ISO 45001:2018 and brand-operator safety frameworks, 'certification does not yet reach across our entire portfolio' and it is still 'extending ISO 45001 certification across our domestic portfolio'. Consequences named: compensation claims, regulatory penalties, operational downtime and reputational damage.

risks.risk: Human-rights and labour risk in an outsourced, migrant-heavy value chain
risks.note: Flagged as a RISK with negative implications: 'Our value chain draws on outsourced laundry, housekeeping, security and construction services, and on migrant workers at our Maldivian resorts - the very places where wage, working-hour and accommodation issues can arise', with rising expectations under BRSR Principle 5, the EU CSDDD and the OECD Guidelines. Violations 'would expose us to regulatory penalties, litigation, brand damage and lost investor confidence'. This compounds the workforce-structure disclosure below.

risks.risk: Workforce structure and attrition - almost the entire workforce is non-permanent
risks.note: A structural concentration visible in the BRSR headcount table rather than labelled as a risk: of 3,108 employees only 38 are permanent, 3,070 are 'other than permanent', and of 3 workers none are permanent - so service delivery in a luxury-service business rests almost entirely on non-permanent and outsourced labour. The Company separately acknowledges 'an industry marked by high attrition' and that women were 19.37% of the workforce in FY 2025-26 against a 30% target by FY 2029-30, with 0 of 3 KMP and 1 of 6 directors being women. Note the reported FY 2025-26 permanent-employee turnover of 2.78% covers only the 38 permanent staff; prior-year comparatives are printed 'NA' because FY 2025-26 is the first BRSR reporting year, so no trend can be read. [Headcount and diversity figures back-filled with provenance from the profile/registry sibling bundles - BRSR Section A.]

risks.risk: Dependence on third-party brand operators and on guest sentiment
risks.note: The Company is an asset owner whose promise 'rests on delivering service of consistent quality across six global brand standards: Marriott, Hilton, Anantara/Minor, Conrad, Oakwood and Atmosphere', and it states plainly that 'online reviews and social sentiment move our RevPAR directly'. Service standards are aligned with brand operators 'on an ongoing basis', i.e. day-to-day guest experience and therefore pricing power sit with counterparties the Company does not control. Note the operator list here (Anantara/Minor, Conrad, Oakwood, Atmosphere) differs from the Corporate Overview's '6 Hospitality Operators' list (Marriott International, Hilton Worldwide, Atmosphere Core, Minor Group, Ascott Hotels, Soho House & Co Inc.) - recorded as printed.

risks.risk: Ecological licence risk at protected coastal and reef locations
risks.note: Several properties 'sit in ecologically sensitive settings - coral-island resorts in the Maldives and coastal properties under Coastal Regulation Zone conditions - where the reef, the shoreline and the silence are the experience. Were these to degrade, we would risk both our construction licences and the very destination magic on which our luxury positioning rests.' Compliance depends on Maldives EPA approvals and CRZ conditions, so both existing operations and the development pipeline carry permit risk.

Flagged as material: 'Our food and beverage operations contribute a significant share of our revenue, and a single food-safety incident at a luxury property can do bra[nd damage]' - the disclosure is truncated mid-sentence in the routed text, so the mitigation column for this topic is unavailable. Relevant given the stated 70+ F&B offerings across the portfolio.

Not labelled a risk by the Company but disclosed structurally: operations span only 3 Indian states and 1 international country (BRSR Section A), the Pune cluster carries six hotels plus all four commercial annuity assets, and the 'social licence to operate matters most around our flagship Pune cluster and the island communities that neighbour our Maldivian resorts'. Two subsidiaries (Nagenahira Resorts, KBJ Hotel & Restaurants) are yet to commence operations, so the Sri Lanka leg is committed capital not yet earning. [Concentration facts back-filled with provenance from the profile/registry sibling bundles.]

risks.risk: Macro, geopolitical and travel-cost sensitivity of discretionary demand
risks.note: The Board's Report and MD&A name geopolitical and economic uncertainty, prolonged conflicts, inflation and financial volatility, high travel costs and a traveller shift toward 'value for money' as factors that may affect travel patterns in 2026; management records that 'global travel demand witnessed periods of uncertainty during the year, influenced by evolving geopolitical developments, including tensions in parts of the Middle East'. India's international tourist arrivals themselves moderated 2.4% to 20.09 Mn in 2025. The cautionary statement adds economic developments, pricing and demand-supply conditions, changes in government regulations, tax laws, litigation and industrial relations as factors that could influence operations. [Macro items back-filled with provenance from the strategy_outlook sibling bundle.]

one-line thesis: Ventive delivered strong Q4FY26 growth with 21% revenue and 28% EBITDA growth despite geopolitical headwinds, driven by premium rate leadership in Pune and Maldives, margin expansion via cost discipline and operational leverage, and a fortified balance sheet enabling disciplined capital allocation — what matters is the platform’s resilience and ability to generate high-teen EBITDA growth even amid travel disruptions.
financial scorecard: revenue: +21% YoY (INR 870cr); EBITDA/margin: +28% YoY to INR 476cr (55% margin); PAT (rptd): >INR 500cr FY26; PAT (normalized): adjusted for INR 74cr FX gain, EBITDA growth was 8% YoY; order book: N/A; net debt: INR 1,484cr (net debt/EBITDA 1.14x, down from 1.7x), reduced via INR 300cr debt paydown and internal accruals — one-offs: Q4 FY26 had INR 5cr electricity debit; Q4 FY25 had INR 8cr government grant and INR 1.5cr electricity credit
guidance: revenue growth: low-teen; margin: sustained high-teen EBITDA growth; order inflow: no new acquisitions announced; capex/commissioning: INR 1,000cr over 3 years for Bangalore AC conversion (Mar27), Varanasi Marriott (FY28), Ritz-Carlton Reserve Sri Lanka (FY28), funded internally
segment / subsidiary detail: India: Q4 revenue +5% YoY to INR 238cr, EBITDA -7% YoY (adjusted +6% to INR 102cr), ADR +12% to INR 14,020, RevPAR +8% to INR 9,634, occupancy 69%; Maldives: Q4 revenue +18% to INR 421cr, EBITDA +19% to INR 198cr, TRevPAR +18% to INR 90,818, occupancy 75%; Annuity: Q4 revenue +2% to INR 127cr, EBITDA +2% to INR 113cr, margin 89%
growth verticals / optionality: Hilton Goa expansion (60-70 new keys), Sol de Goa integration, Soho House Delhi (2-year timeline), Raaya all-inclusive scaling, Narmada Estates annuity development, potential branded residences at Batim Land
margins & cost dynamics: India: margin expansion to 43% in Q4 via ADR-led leverage despite occupancy dip; Maldives: margin up to 47% via occupancy gain + solar/cluster procurement cost controls; overall hospitality EBITDA margin up 300bps to 37% in FY26
capex / expansion: INR 1,000cr over 3 years: Bangalore AC Marriott (INR 300cr, Mar27), Varanasi Marriott (INR 400cr, FY28), Ritz-Carlton Reserve Sri Lanka (INR 300cr, FY28), FF&E, Sol de Goa integration — fully funded by internal accruals
capital allocation: Prioritized debt reduction (INR 300cr paydown), strategic acquisitions (Hilton Goa, Soho House — INR 200cr), capex funding, and annuity land acquisition (Narmada Estates); no external funding planned; net debt/EBITDA down to 1.14x
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical travel disruptions (Middle East, source market volatility), diesel supply constraints in Maldives, occupancy recovery lag in India post-disruption, execution risk in capex projects, currency volatility on USD debt
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and resilient — management emphasized platform strength, asset quality over scale, internal funding, and long-term margin expansion; dismissed short-term noise, highlighted Pune and Maldives as structural growth engines
non-obvious takeaways: Pune’s luxury ADRs now match gateway cities despite limited international connectivity, driven by Japan/Korea manufacturing business travel; Maldives demand is shifting from China/Russia to Europe/Australia with shorter booking windows; Raaya’s all-inclusive model is expanding customer base without diluting luxury positioning

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

summary.Top Anchor: QUANT MUTUAL FUND - QUANT SMALL CAP FUND

hero.oneLiner: Ventive Hospitality is an ownership-led hospitality platform promoted by Panchshil Realty and Blackstone, owning a portfolio of luxury and business hotels and resorts across India, the Maldives and Sri Lanka, complemented by integrated commercial and retail annuity space in Pune.
